rows.note: This is the all-purpose term for a relapse, including a drug relapse.

example.english: They had been off drugs for months, but recently had a relapse, and their family is very worried.
example.traditional: 佢戒咗毒幾個月，最近又復發，屋企人都好擔心。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gaai3 zo2 duk6 gei2 go3 jyut6 zeoi3 gan6 jau6 fuk6 faat3 uk1 kei2 jan4 dou1 hou2 daam1 sam1

rows.note: Use this colloquial alternative especially when an illness or addiction starts again after improving.

example.english: I thought my eczema was gone, but it had a relapse last night.
example.traditional: 我以為濕疹好返晒，點知尋晚又翻發。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ji5 wai4 sap1 can2 hou2 faan1 saai3 dim2 zi1 cam4 maan5 jau6 faan1 faat3

rows.note: Use this for a disease or medical condition that becomes active or worse again after improving.

example.english: The illness had just improved, but it began to relapse.
example.traditional: 佢啱啱好返，點知病情又復發。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ngaam1 ngaam1 hou2 faan1 dim2 zi1 beng6 cing4 jau6 fuk6 faat3

rows.note: Use this when someone or something slips back into its former bad state or pattern.

example.english: Without anyone keeping an eye on him, he can relapse into his old bad habits and be late every day.
example.traditional: 一冇人睇住，佢就打回原形，成日遲到。
example.jyutping: jat1 mou5 jan4 tai2 zyu6 keoi5 zau6 daa2 wui4 jyun4 jing4 seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3

rows.note: Use this colloquial pattern when someone resumes a former addictive or self-harming behavior, with the context making the relapse clear.

example.english: After quitting smoking for months, he began to relapse and smoke again whenever he felt stressed.
example.traditional: 佢戒咗煙幾個月，一有壓力就又食返煙。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gaai3 zo2 jin1 gei2 go3 jyut6 jat1 jau5 aat3 lik6 zau6 jau6 sik6 faan2 jin1
